title: VibeGraph quality layer: evidence vocabulary
description: Run 2 of the quality-layer brief (reviews/quality-layer/BRIEF.md, Part D). The shared definitions every other quality schema references: the five provenance kinds, the explicit Unknown, node references, the cost classes, and the CheckResult shape in which a pass MUST carry what it could not follow and no verdict can be a bare boolean. Nothing here is a config; it is the vocabulary configs are written in. Two provenance kinds can never enter a deterministic gate (model_judgement, self_report) and the schema says so with a const, not a comment.

ProvenanceKind.description: Who is speaking. derived: a script over source, manifests or the IR. stated: a human, the orchestrator's confirmed brief, or an agent over MCP, with the record id. observed: a trace run (the overlay beside the IR, never in it). model_judgement: a model's verdict, with the model and prompt hash. self_report: a worker's own summary, labelled and never load-bearing.

by.description: The deriving module or script, e.g. thread_contract.ts, scripts/derive_stack_profile.mjs.

commit.description: The repository commit the derivation read.

id.description: The constraint, policy or ruling id that states it.

stale.description: Per-file staleness as the observations store decides it; a stale observation may inform, never gate.

model.description: The audit label already used by PacketReview.model, e.g. claude:claude-opus-5.

entersGate.description: A model's verdict never rewrites a check's verdict and never enters a deterministic gate.

GateProvenance.description: The only provenances a deterministic gate may read. Structurally excludes model_judgement and self_report.

Unknown.description: A value that could not be derived and was not stated. Carries its reason. Never a plausible default.

NodeId.description: The IR's structural node id grammar (schemas/ir.schema.json NodeId).

NodeRef.description: file:node, the form every offender and every supporting node takes, so a reject is actionable.

FileOrNodeRef.description: Either a project-relative file path or a file:node reference. The file part must contain a slash or a dot, so a bare name (`SCHEMA`) is refused as an operand; a file with no extension and no directory cannot be told from a bare name here and is left to the verb's precondition (both operands must resolve to something the IR had).

CostClass.description: Derived from a check's decision procedure, never asserted. local: one function subtree. thread: one thread traversal. delta: the packet's diffs only. graph: project-wide. observed: needs the trace overlay.

UnverifiableCause.description: Why the IR could not answer. dynamic: runtime dispatch that could be the target or guard (only observed or stated evidence lifts it). unresolved: a resolution gap the linker owes (a re-link may lift it). precondition: the verb is outside its competence here. no-such-name: the operand names nothing the IR knows. not-yet: a run-level check whose requiring packet has not run.

notFollowed.description: What the check did NOT verify. Never empty: a pass that followed everything is a claim no static check can make.

offenders.description: Never empty: a violation with no offender is not actionable and is refused.

at.description: The terminals or nodes that made it unverifiable. May be empty for precondition and no-such-name.

CheckResult.description: Three verdicts, never two, never a boolean.
